{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement between an organoid model and human clinical outcomes for drug-induced liver injury (Sensitivity: 88.7%, Specificity: 88.9%).",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "We successfully developed an organoid based assay with multiplexed readouts measuring viability, cholestatic and/or mitochondrial toxicity with high predictive values for 238 marketed drugs",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Preclinical identification of compounds at risk of causing drug induced liver injury (DILI) remains a significant challenge in drug development",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "Here, we established a human liver organoid (HLO)-based screening model for analyzing DILI pathology at organoid resolution.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study uses human pluripotent stem cell-derived organoids and compares their predictive value to marketed drugs, without reference to specific animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "measuring viability, cholestatic and/or mitochondrial toxicity with high predictive values for 238 marketed drugs"
}
